title: How the dance orchestra gets work; the union and being sick
summary: Orchestra jobs come through pleasure clubs and balls rather than the union; the union gives sick members an occasional job.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well now I wonder about, is it, I mean your orchestra, do they get many jobs through organizations?
Well practically all the jobs they get me through organizations. You see if it's a funeral.
No I mean the orchestra, the dance orchestra.

Oh the dance orchestra? Well they get that through organizations too. They get it through pleasure clubs. It's like this season all the balls is going on. They're hiring whatever band they want for balls. And people giving dances, public dances, they hire. Organizations giving a public dance or pleasure club or anything and they know it, they'll hire. I mean that's all the contact you have. You see the only thing that's pointless here in Northern which you know that is burdensome to the quality. If you don't get out there you don't have nothing pointless. And all the other jobs come from the outside. Anybody that know the orchestra, know someone in the orchestra, want their type of music, you hire. Some people want rock and roll, some want progressive, some want Dixieland, but it all comes through different categories. Now you take like out the country club, they don't want nothing but Dixieland there. See? So I mean that's the contact the musicians have. We don't get anything through the union in the line of jobs unless somebody particularly asks for a certain band.
Maybe a little project once in a while. Just a project, yeah.

Well I mean that's the thing. And you don't get that for about once a year. I mean they have so many members and then they be trying to help, you know, help one another out. You know one probably get all up and the other one don't get none. Now what they will do, like I'm sick, they'll give me one because that helps me. I have to keep my card and thing up. Which I get my card about a year, you see. I never have got a quarter card since I've been in it. I always get my card about a year. But like I'm sick and handicapped now, that helps me out. I don't have anything, anything coming in.

Anything coming in on a person down sick out. See? Because I don't have, I don't have no way of making a living. Now before I had a living because I could work and I could play music too. See, I don't have no way of doing that.
